$comment: Executable receipts for the numbers this repository publishes in prose. Run with `verify-claims --root . run` (alloevil/verify-claims); CI runs it via .github/workflows/claims.yml. Each check runs scripts/setup.sh first, which pins chenglou/handwired at 257856e.

claims.claim: Every spike runs against chenglou/handwired pinned at commit 257856e.
claims.method: setup.sh clones upstream and checks out the pinned commit; git prints HEAD.

claims.claim: In the R2R EWMA circuit (40 runs per lot, 1,718 live operations), the reference and compiled evaluators differ in 0 of 3,840 outputs.
claims.metric: bitwise comparison of evaluateReference and createTensorEvaluator outputs

claims.claim: Gradient training through the circuit lowers test MSE from 293.39 (hand-tuned lambda=0.3, g=1/9) to 185.81 (lambda=0.7881, g=0.1110) on synthetic lots.
claims.metric: mean squared error vs target on 16 held-out synthetic lots
claims.method: Adam on dL/dlambda and dL/dg from backpropagateReference, 300 steps x 16 training lots.

contains: hand-tuned lambda=0.3 g=1/B_NOM=0.1111: train MSE 288.90, test MSE 293.39
gradient-trained: lambda=0.7881 g=0.1110 train MSE 189.40, test MSE 185.81

claims.claim: A 12,120-evaluation fine grid lands on the same optimum (train MSE 189.40) as gradient training; the coarse 2,050-evaluation grid stops at lambda=0.78, g=0.1120 (train MSE 206.61, test MSE 202.64).
claims.metric: train MSE at the best grid point
claims.method: Plain JS grid search over lambda and g.

contains: fine grid (12120 evals): lambda=0.790 g=0.1110 MSE 189.40
grid search (2050 evals, 50x41): lambda=0.78 g=0.1120 train MSE 206.61, test MSE 202.64

claims.claim: A threshold compared with emitCompare gets zero gradient at all three probe points, as issue #1 reports.
claims.metric: d alarm / d thr from backpropagateReference

claims.claim: Across 300 seeded random programs x 40 inputs in two build modes, reference and compiled evaluators never differ.
Written with roundAffine, the circuit equals step-by-step Math.fround JS on all 113,480 values.
claims.metric: first mismatch vs JS-fround in roundAffine mode
claims.method: spikes/diff-fuzz.ts records the first mismatch; null means none.

contains: first roundAffine mismatch vs JS-fround: null

claims.claim: Written with plain affine, 2,246 of 113,480 values (1.98%) differ from step-by-step fround JS, because the builder merges small affine sums.
claims.metric: count of values differing from JS-fround in affine mode
claims.method: Same fuzz run, affine build mode.

claims.claim: Against plain float64 JS, 55,336 of 113,480 roundAffine values differ (48.8%); median relative error 2.59e-8, p99 1.86e-7, 2 values above 1e-3.
claims.metric: values differing from float64 JS, roundAffine mode
claims.method: Same fuzz run; relative error over differing finite values.

contains: median 2.59e-8, p99 1.86e-7; >1e-3 (gross, e.g. branch flip or underflow): 2

claims.claim: affine(affine(x)) differs from step-by-step fround JS at 4,336 of 10,000 points; 2 built operations become 1 live one.
Backprop gradients match central differences of the float64 JS program in 3,000 of 3,000 cases (worst relative error 2.06e-7).
claims.method: spikes/grad-check.ts on 200 random programs x 5 points x 3 inputs.

claims.claim: At 257856e, handwired's own `bun run test` reported 1,347 tests: 1,345 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail.
claims.method: Ran once in vendor/handwired with Bun 1.4.2 on Linux x64 (about 371 s).

check.manual: the upstream suite takes about 6 minutes and tests upstream code, not this repository; rerun by hand with the repro command
